name: Lead titanate / strontium titanate superlattice
equilibrium_context: Ferroelectric superlattice with a/c domains or polar vortex structures; the supercrystal phase does not exist in the equilibrium phase diagram

driven_states.emergent_property: Sub-picosecond light pulses transform the superlattice into a coherent three-dimensional supercrystal phase with polar, strain and charge order periodicity up to 30 nanometers. The state persists indefinitely under ambient conditions and can be erased thermally.
driven_states.source: Stoica, Laanait, Dai et al., Nature Materials 18, 377 (2019), doi:10.1038/s41563-019-0311-x
driven_states.caveat: Genuine, indefinitely long-lived metastability at room temperature - one of only two such cases in the registry. The mechanism (photoinduced charge carriers, screening of the depolarization field, electrostriction) is, however, not clarified. The state is tied to the heterostructure, not to a bulk material, and is strongly sample-dependent.

threshold.quantity: fluence threshold plus accumulation over many pulses

sources: Stoica et al., Nature Materials 18, 377 (2019), doi:10.1038/s41563-019-0311-x
